result:
I've written the plan for w126 (`work request` and its parts, requests r1–r5) and marked the work-item `DONE` with no open questions for the person.

All five scenarios fail today for the same reasons: nothing connects `features/requests.feature` to step definitions, `scripts/work` has no `request`, `outcome` or `turn` command, and nothing in `scripts/` writes a request. I settled the researcher's six questions in the plan:

- **r4 and r5:** their scenarios run `work outcome` and `work turn`, so this work-item adds both, doing exactly what r15 and r7 say. Refusing a command run out of turn and changing the status on a turn (r16–r18) stay with w127. As a result, w127's r15 and r7 scenarios may already pass when it runs.
- **Commit:** `work request` doesn't commit yet, because r12 belongs to w128. Every check runs before anything is written, so a refused request changes nothing. The test repositories are still set up as git repositories, so the same tests hold once w128 adds commits.
- **Where the request is written:** in the repository `work` runs on, given by its existing `--root` option, under `.shop/work/requests/q<n>.md`. There is no new option.
- **Printed id:** `q<n>`, the way `work add` prints `w<n>`. The file itself keeps the full `request/<context path>/q<n>`.
- **Form of `lines.md`:** each text line of the file is one line of the request, in order, numbered from 1.
- **Strict-form check:** done with the existing Python check (`model_parse.ears`), so `work` doesn't need clingo.
- **The `model check` defect:** `model check` reports any `.shop/work/requests/` directory as a missing initiative. That fix, and design-model-check's 13 failing request scenarios, stay with w131.

The files that change are `scripts/work`, a new `scripts/workqueue_request.py`, `CLAUDE.md` (one module-map row for the new module, which I added to the researcher's list), and two new test files, `tests/scenarios/test_requests.py` and `tests/scenarios/requests_steps.py`.

No existing test should break. That rests on the researcher's text search, because there was no coverage map to check against, so the implementer should run the whole suite once the scenarios pass. Separately, the researcher found that pytest's `--work-item w126` option aborts collection while no w126 scenario exists. Once `requests.feature` is connected to tests, that abort should go away for w126. Edge cases the scenarios don't cover are listed in the plan for the implementer.

Files are in `.shop/scratch/2-plan/`:
- `plan.md`
- `result.json`
